title: 2026-06-02 POC Weekly Sync - Reliability Incident Followup
summary: Weekly POC sync to review last week's reliability incidents (timeouts, 5xxs, rate limits) and agree on next steps. SE reviewed logs and root cause: autoscaler bug + upstream rate-limiter misconfiguration; mitigation: clients to enable exponential backoff and retries, Redwood to patch autoscaler and provide hotspot routing. Agreed to run a controlled load test next Tue and share full request/response traces. Customer considering Dedicated pool if incidents persist.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-02 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alice Morgan (Redwood AE), Ben Park (Redwood SE), Ravi Singh (Redwood CSM), Cara Thompson (BrightEdge ML), David Lopez (BrightEdge SRE), Mina Patel (BrightEdge PM)

Summary (auto): follow-up on reliability incident last week where multiple client requests hit 5xxs and timeouts during traffic spike; discussed root cause, immediate mitigations, and next steps.

00:00 Alice Morgan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep to 45 minutes, quick recap from last week's incident then ben will walk through logs
00:18 Cara Thompson: yep thanks, we got hit on Tuesday at 10:12AM our time, about 20% of requests saw 5xxs and a bunch of timeouts, some spikes in latency too
00:35 Ben Park: yeah we pulled the traces, there are a couple of things overlapping, autoscaler didn't react because of a race in the scale down/scale up path, then the upstream rate limiter started returning 429s and a few of those were mistakenly mapped to 5xx by our stack — so you see 5xx in the dashboard
00:52 David Lopez: can you explain that mapping again? our infra sees 503s and 5xx from your endpoint, but we also have an internal rate limit at the edge, might be double limiting
01:10 Ben Park: right, so two things: one, the internal rate limiter at your side was configured tighter than expected on that route; two, when the autoscaler hit a transient error we had a retry flapping that caused short overload, and some internal proxies surfaced it as 502/503. transcription note: sometimes our logs say kv-cache, sometimes k-v cache in the trace
01:40 Cara Thompson: we also saw a lot of retries from our clients, which probably amplified the spike — we used simple fixed backoff not exponential
01:55 Alice Morgan: ok so mitigation path A: client side changes (exponential backoff + jitter, cap retries), mitigation path B: server side (hotfix to autoscaler, improve error codes so 429 propagates as 429), path C: rate-limit tuning / hotspot routing. ben, can you walk through the logs you mentioned?
02:12 Ben Park: sure, uploading screen now — so here's a snippet from 10:11:58 to 10:13:30, you can see request QPS jump from 120 to 900 within 90s, TTL on KV cache wasn't warmed for some long tails so backend latency jumped which triggered scaling, but because of a bug scaling decreased capacity briefly then scaled up leading to a short window of underprovisioning
02:40 Mina Patel: that matches our load spike window, we had a marketing spike from a campaign, surprised it was that big though
02:54 David Lopez: side question, are those retried calls counted against our application quota? we count per-request regardless of retry at the current setup
03:10 Ben Park: yes retries count, which is why client-side retry behavior matters. we recommended a 5s exponential backoff with max 3 retries and jitter, that reduced effective QPS by about 30% in our tests
03:28 Cara Thompson: about the 5xx mapping — will you make sure 429 is preserved? it messes with our incident detection which alerts on 5xx > 5%
03:42 Ben Park: absolutely, it's on the patch list. the immediate change will be to preserve upstream status codes, second will be explicit rate-limit headers so you get Retry-After. noted that some proxies normalize codes today, we'll add docs for the proxy mapping
04:02 Alice Morgan: we also talked about rate limits per route, small burst allowance and a per-customer token bucket, ben can you outline routing options if we split into hotspot routing for this route?
04:18 Ben Park: yeah hotspot routing is basically pinning high QPS keys to a warm pool, bypassing cold start scaling. for POC we can config a small dedicated warm pool for your campaign endpoints. if that still causes incidents we recommend Dedicated capacity with reserved GPUs — more predictable throughput and SLA
04:38 Mina Patel: what is the delta cost for the Dedicated suggestion? rough numbers are fine now
04:46 Alice Morgan: i'll put an initial sizing and cost estimate in the next steps, naive guess is an extra monthly reserve for the campaign windows, but we'll be specific once ben gives the QPS profile
04:58 David Lopez: observability: can you enable full request/response traces for the test window only? we don't want PII or payloads stored long term
05:12 Ben Park: yes we can, will redact payload and provide structured traces and timestamps. we'll share a presigned secure s3 link with logs. also we'll add sampling headers to correlate client id to traces
05:28 Cara Thompson: one technical ask — do you support prefix/KV cache warming APIs? we want to pre-warm top keys before campaign goes live
05:40 Ben Park: there is a cache pre-warm API but it's non-public by default; for POC we'll enable it in staging and show a runbook. caveat: warms need to be sized to avoid evicting other hot keys
05:55 Mina Patel: in terms of security/compliance, we need SOC 2 evidence and SAML SSO integration for the teams that will access logs
06:10 Alice Morgan: we have SOC 2 Type II docs and we'll share the security packet; SAML SSO is supported, RBAC can be scoped to your org, and KMS integration is available for Private deployments
06:25 David Lopez: any impact on data residency if we turn on full traces? we are EU-only customer for personal data, logs should remain in eu-west region if possible
06:38 Ben Park: yes we can scope storage regionally for traces and logs. we'll ensure redaction rules and region in the trace export
06:50 Cara Thompson: ok good. operationally, how should we change alerts to avoid noisy paging during a transient? we don't want to silence important alerts though
07:05 Alice Morgan: two changes: change alerting thresholds to account for expected retry amplification, and add a short suppression window for known campaign windows; ben will share recommended Prometheus alert rules and pagerduty runbook edits
07:22 Ben Park: also recommend tracking token-level cost and per-route latency in the console so you have a quick page to correlate spikes with campaign ids
07:35 Cara Thompson: timeline and responsibilities? we need a clarification for our internal stakeholders by EOD Friday if possible
07:44 Alice Morgan: agreed — we will get the patch diff and logs by Thursday, test plan by Monday, estimate for Dedicated by Sunday, and the controlled load test is scheduled for 2026-06-09 10:00 PST
07:58 Ravi Singh: i'll own the run of the load test and share an invite and test plan; will also coordinate canary rollout for the autoscaler patch with ben
08:12 David Lopez: one more — what about rate limit header semantics, you said you'd expose Retry-After and X-RateLimit-Remaining?
08:22 Ben Park: yes we'll add X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, and Retry-After; for the POC we'll keep short TTLs and adjust as we learn
08:35 Cara Thompson: any mention of competitors? we evaluated Anthropic and Vertex but they had higher cost per token for our dataset and limited dedicated-pool options
08:49 Alice Morgan: ok final recap: Ben to share logs and patch diff, Cara to provide traffic samples, Ravi to schedule load test, Alice to share Dedicated estimate and security docs. We'll reconvene after the controlled load test to review metrics and decide on next steps including Dedicated purchase if needed.
09:05 Alice Morgan: thanks all, we'll follow up in email; meeting adjourned
notes: Autoscaler race condition identified as primary root cause of underprovisioning window
Client retries amplified spike — recommended exponential backoff with jitter and capped retries
Preserve upstream 429s and add rate-limit headers to improve observability
Enable pre-warm cache API in staging for campaign endpoints
